chunks: And when it was said to them: 'Live in this land and eat of its produce wheresoever you like, and ask for remission of your sins, but pass through the gates with submission (and not pride), We shall forgive your trespasses, and give to those who are righteous abundance,'

key_terms.الْقَرْيَةَ: The city, specifically referring to Jerusalem in this context
key_terms.الْمُحْسِنِينَ: The doers of good, those who are righteous and virtuous
key_terms.حِطَّةٌ: A word of remission or forgiveness, often recited upon entering a place
key_terms.سُجَّداً: In a state of prostration, indicating humility and submission

ai.seo_question: What was the specific command given to the Children of Israel regarding their entry into Jerusalem and the condition for their forgiveness?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-A'raf recounts the divine command given to the Children of Israel upon their entry into Jerusalem. God instructed them to reside in the city, eat freely from its provisions, and demonstrate humility by entering the gate prostrating while reciting 'Hittah' (remission of sins), promising forgiveness and increased bounty for those who were righteous.
